name: cmux.newtab/1
docs: A whole New Tab page: the app's scene is the page's body, in place of cmux's own page. It shows only when the person names the app in the setting tabs.newTabApp (Settings > Tabs > New Tab App); unset, cmux draws its own page, unchanged. When the named app is missing, disabled, hidden or its render fails, cmux draws its own page. The render export gets the mount context ({surface: "newTab", cwd?}: the folder the new tab starts in). It mounts once per New Tab page and stays mounted while the page lives, also behind another tab; it unmounts when the tab becomes something else. Clicks run the node's onTap with the app's own scopes: open the tab the person wants with cmux.actions.run from a click (actions:run). The web New Tab page draws it; the native New Tab page (tabs.nativeNewTabPage) does not. Its scene can hold Composer({prompt?, placeholder?, cwd?}): cmux draws its own New Tab composer there (the project and agent chips, attachments, slash commands, the start flow), and that field takes the keys typed after Cmd-T; prompt puts the Console's `>` before a monospace field, cwd moves the folder the next chat starts in. A node's .opens({chat: key}) or .opens({closed: id}) opens that chat, or reopens that Recently Closed item, in the New Tab's own tab as the person's click, through cmux's own path, with no app scope. A recent-chats list reads chat.list with a limit (the newest N, never every chat sorted); Icon("harness:<id>") draws an agent's own mark.
status: draft: shapes are refined with the first implementing app before the interface is public
